primary_diagnosis_treated: Hyperkalaemia / metabolic acidosis (stage‑5 CKD) with hypertension, diabetes and anemia

medications.medication: Humulin (insulin isophane 70 U/mL + regular 30 U/mL) mixed suspension
medications.dose: Patient‑specific dosing; titrate to target glucose
medications.purpose: Management of diabetes mellitus in CKD
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes control is essential in CKD (NICE NG203 recommends optimisation of glycaemia)
BP target <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if proteinuric) per NICE NG203

medications.duration: Titrate to target BP over 4‑6 weeks, then lifelong — review annually
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin blockade to reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: First‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension (NG203, first_line_treatment)

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: Statin recommended for all CKD patients (NG203, first_line_treatment)

medications.dose: 8.4 g PO once daily mixed with water
medications.duration: Until serum K⁺ ≤5.0 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Chronic hyperkalaemia management to enable ACE‑I therapy
medications.nice_justification: Not in NG203 but endorsed by KDIGO for chronic K⁺ control; required to safely use ACE‑I in CKD

medications.dose: 200 mg PO three times daily with vitamin C
medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >30 %, then review
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends iron supplementation after anemia screening in CKD stage 4‑5

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ACE‑I dose
interactions_checked.action: Start Ramipril at 1.25 mg, monitor BP and symptoms; consider reducing HCTZ if BP <100/60 mmHg

interactions_checked.interaction: Patiromer can bind oral medications; insulin is injected but timing may affect glucose monitoring adherence
interactions_checked.action: Take patiromer at least 30 min after insulin injection and separate from other oral meds

interactions_checked.interaction: Patiromer may reduce absorption of oral iron
interactions_checked.action: Administer iron at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after patiromer

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant interaction with current meds

contraindications.reason: eGFR 13.6 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
eGFR <20 mL/min/1.73 m² – outside approved indication (NICE TA775)
contraindications.alternative: No SGLT2 inhibitor at this renal function

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure not recorded – obtain measurement before titrating Ramipril and adjust antihypertensive regimen accordingly.
Serum potassium not available – obtain baseline K⁺ before starting patiromer and ACE‑I; monitor 48 h after initiation and weekly until stable.
Liver function tests not available – obtain ALT/AST/bilirubin before starting atorvastatin.
Lipid profile not available – obtain baseline LDL‑C to confirm need for statin and future titration.
Iron studies (Hb, ferritin, TSAT) not available – order before initiating ferrous sulfate.
Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not recorded – needed to confirm proteinuria severity and BP target.
Allergy status unknown – verify no allergy to ACE‑I, statin, iron, or patiromer before prescribing.
Smoking status unknown – assess and provide cessation support if current smoker.
Weight/BMI not recorded – required for insulin dose adjustments and sodium bicarbonate dosing if needed.
treatment_summary: The plan adds renin‑angiotensin blockade (Ramipril) and a high‑intensity statin (Atorvastatin) as first‑line CKD interventions per NICE NG203, introduces patiromer to control chronic hyperkalaemia and enable ACE‑I use, and provides oral iron for CKD‑related anemia. Existing insulin and hydrochlorothiazide are continued. All drug choices respect contraindications (no metformin, NSAIDs, ACE‑I/ARB combo, or SGLT2 inhibitor) and interactions are managed with timing advice and BP monitoring. Missing laboratory and clinical data are flagged for acquisition before initiation.
